Parks and Recreation Commission Meeting Minutes January 14, 2026 Little Rock City Hall Attendance: Ben France, Quinten Whiteside, Mike Bernardo, Cannon Fletcher, Summer Campbell, Chemia Woods, Amber Tiegen, Nolan Hughes Absent: Samuel Ellis City Board of Director Liaison: City Director-Capi Peck, City Director-Andrea Lewis LRPR/LRCAO Staff: Parks Director-Leland Couch, Deputy Director Administration-Angela Nelson, Deputy Director Operations-Justin Dorsey, Deputy Director of Recreations-Shawanda Craig, Deputy City Attorney-Simone Blagg, Safety and Training Coordinator-Courtney Perry, Administrative Assistant to the Parks Director-Mahoganey Burkhalter, Parks Data and Marketing Coordinator-Graham Brown, Secretary-Kyndall Richardson Welcome: Chairman France welcomed everyone. Meeting called to order at 11:51 am. Roll Call: Roll call completed. Seven (7) Commissioners present. Quorum was established. Approval of Minutes: Chairman France asked for a motion to approve January 2026 minutes. Vice Chairman Whiteside made 1st motion. Motion was 2nd by Commissioner Campbell. Vote passed. Motion carried. Citizen Communication: None Director’s Presentation/Staff Reports/Events: Staff Reports: ❖ Commissioner Fletcher – asked about Organizational Safety report. o Coordinator Courtney Perry discussed the breakdown in his report. ❖ Commissioner Woods – asked about the open Social Media Specialist position & asked for more data regarding Parks employee management processes. o Director Couch discussed where they were in hiring and asked Coordinator Graham Brown to give information regarding who they were using to fulfill the role. Deputy Director Angela Nelson discussed the employment process and will provide more information at the next meeting in February. Director’s Report: ❖ BOD Items: o Otter Creek Soccer field Contract o Pedestrian Bridge project o 30 Crossing project o ELR facility lease o Saferooms project 1 o Natural Stepps lease expansion o MacArthur Dog Park ❖ Coordinator-Graham Brown – In the process of working on Accreditation for Parks and will apply in Spring 2026. ❖ New Commissioner Introductions. o Amber Tiegen o Nolan Hughes Events: ❖ State of the City – January 22nd ❖ Deck Park - Community Engagement Meeting – January 22nd ❖ Disc Golf Course event – January 31st Presentation: ❖ Presentation – Parks Director Leland Couch – 30 Crossing Unfinished Business: ❖ Subcommittee Reports o Masterplan Subcommittee Report– Commissioner Fletcher - No Masterplan Subcommittee meeting was held. No update at this time. o Marketing Subcommittee Report –Vice Chairman Whiteside had No Update. They weren’t able to meet. o Parks Conservancy Subcommittee Report – Subcommittee Chair – Commissioner Ellis was absent today. Parks Director attended and gave an update. ❖ Presentation list discussion/Selection for the next meeting. o Wasn’t discussed, we will add an update later based on what was requested during the course of the meeting. ❖ Subcommittee Assignments/Subcommittee Chair/ Subcommittee Chair Procedure. o Subcommittees and the process were explained to the new Commissioners. No new assignments at this time. ❖ Commissioner Retreat Dates – Deputy City Atty Blagg. o Chairman France asked about the Facilitator. Discussed their role for the upcoming retreat. An Agenda for the retreat was requested. ❖ Chair – Vice Chair Discussion – Election o Will table until New Business. ❖ Vacancy Discussion/Commissioner Ellis Update/Commissioner Knight Removal o Discussed addition of new Commissioners and encouraged the Commissioners to continue getting the information out about the vacancies on the Parks Commission. 2 ❖ Parks Commission Presentation to the BOD o Chairman France discussed what was presented to them previously by Coordinator Brown at the last meeting and how helpful it was. New Business: ❖ Vote for Retreat Day being on January 28, 2026 o Commissioner Whiteside made a motion to have the Retreat on January 28, 2026. o Commissioner Fletcher asked about why the meeting wasn’t an official meeting. o Commissioner Whiteside restated the motion. 2nd by Commissioner Campbell. Vote Passed. Motion Carried ❖ BOD Presentation – (Does this need to be moved to a later date) o Commissioner Bernardo made a statement about what the BOD presentation is. o Commissioner Whiteside asked if the BOD presentation date has been confirmed. Deputy Atty Blagg was absent. Asst. Mahoganey Burkhalter advised that she will get confirmation on that. ❖ Commissioner Cannon Fletcher - Request to make Dashboard presentation. Will have to be submitted to Parks prior to meeting. o Commissioner Bernardo discussed the Dashboard and what it shows. o Commissioner Fletcher delivered a presentation on a Dashboard that he created. He pulled data from the reports. ❖ Commissioner Kemp Resignation. Thank you for your service. You will be missed! ❖ Commissioner Mike Bernardo last meeting, parting words. Thank you for your hard work and service. You will be missed! ❖ Chairman Ben France last meeting, parting words. Thank you for your hard work and service. You will be missed! ❖ Chair/Vice Chair Election o Commissioner Whiteside nominated himself for Chair. 2nd by Commissioner Woods. Vote passed. Motion passed. o Commissioner Fletcher nominated Commissioner Woods for Vice Chair. 2nd by Commissioner Whiteside. Vote Passed. Motion carried. o New Chair of Parks Commission is Quinten Whiteside. New Vice Chair of Parks Commission is Chemia Woods. Congratulations!!! Agenda items for next meeting: ❖ Commissioner Woods asked about an ongoing update about the 30 Crossing. Director Couch extended an invite to join the Masterplan Subcommittee. ❖ Commissioner Fletcher – extended an invitation to join the Masterplan Subcommittee. Director Couch asked if an agenda can be sent to Asst. Burkhalter prior to the meeting. 3 Board – liaison Feedback ❖ City Director Andrea Lewis welcomed the new Commissioners and praised the outgoing Commissioners for their commitment and hard work. Parks Commission Recreation - Report 1/14/2026 ALL Community Centers Basketball teams were practicing until the school break. Each center held their Christmas events during the week of December 15 - 19, 2025. Southwest Community Center Letters to Santa (Dec. 1–20): Youth participated in a holiday-themed literacy activity promoting creativity and family engagement. Dunbar Community Center Partnered with DHNA to do a food giveaway on Tuesday, December 23rd from 11am-1pm. Potluck delivered 1500 lbs. of food and plastic bags to be given out to citizens. Special Events: Special Events held: 1) Southwest: Open House & Panthers Cookout (Dec. 4): Open House (Dec. 8); Lotería Night (Dec. 12); Brunch with Santa (Dec. 13). These events strengthened community engagement, increased center visibility, and promoted ongoing programming. 2) West Central: December Coat Drive to give to Dunbar Community Center for the Warming Shelter. The Coat drive ended December 30, 2025. They are to help the ones that come to Center for the shelter and need the assistance. 3) West Central held their 2nd annual Jamboree Youth Basketball games on December 27; there were 10 games played. Youth Athletics Basketball registration closure was on Dec. 19th. • Basketball – Participation and attendance in community centers Registration 2025 – 402 Current 2026 – 411 Increase- ~2% Therapeutic Recreation The 12th Annual TR Christmas Program took place on December 18th. This event is hosted by WLR Fellowship Bible Church- Embrace Special Needs Ministry. There were 17 participants in this year’s cast, originally 19 in the cast but two were out with illness. There were approximately 100 attendees in the audience. Great success! The TR Volunteer Crew, which is made up of members of the Branch Out Program, once again hosted a Blanket Drive in conjunction with Chloe’s Cozy Drive. 40 blankets were donated and will be delivered to the City’s Homeless Services Division for distribution to those in need. MacArthur Museum Special Events – Average 2 special events each month. Baseline 2024 – 24 special events Goal 2025 – 24 special events Current 2025 (January – December) – 48 special events (200% of goal) 1 Parks Commission – Recreation Report Dunbar Community Center After School Programs The after-school program at Dunbar Community Center wrapped up this month. Youth enjoyed our annual holiday meal on December 19th and received gifts from the center. Gifts included stuffed animals, games of their choice and Christmas pencils. We will start registration for the second semester on the 2nd of January online. Youth Basketball Program This month we continued practicing basketball our season starts in January 2026. No practices were held during the LRSD Christmas break. Free Play During the last two weeks of the month the center was open to all youth to attend for free play in the gym. Staff were on hand to keep the youth safe and interacted with them. Special Event We partnered with DHNA to do a food giveaway on Tuesday, December 23rd from 11am-1pm. Potluck delivered 1500 lbs. of food and plastic bags to be given out to citizens. Southwest Community Center Youth Programs: Letters to Santa (Dec. 1–20): Youth participated in a holiday-themed literacy activity promoting creativity and family engagement. Winter Break Camp: Dec 22–Jan 2, 7:30 a.m.–5 p.m. Closed December 25, 2025 & January 1, 2026. The camp has 12 youth registered. Field trips, daily meals, and indoor/outdoor recreation activities are finalized including a sculpture scavenger hunt in the River Market District, a visit to the AGFC Nature Center, and a festive “Noon” Year’s Eve celebration with our friends at Dee Brown Library. . Afterschool & Engagement: Youth participation remained steady through supervised open play and enrichment activities prior to winter break. Dance Program: Continued through early December, average Attendance: 5–10 participants on Tuesdays & Thursdays, 5:30–6:30 p.m. Monthly Fee: $10 per participant Youth Athletics: Basketball Program (Pre-Season Practices Only): Focused on drills, fundamentals, conditioning, and team development across 6U, 8U, 10U, and 12U divisions. League play begins January 2026. Cheer Program (Practice Phase): Participants continued routine development and skill preparation for the upcoming basketball season. Adult Fitness Programs Southwest Steppers (Dance Workout): Average Attendance: 8 participants on Tuesdays & Thursdays, 6:00–7:00 p.m. Program remains staff-led while a volunteer instructor is being sought. 2 Low-Impact Senior Workout: A video-based program serving approximately 15 older adults, providing safe and consistent physical activity. Pickleball: Interest and feasibility continue to be evaluated; no program was launched in December. Special Events & Community Outreach Open House & Panthers Cookout (Dec. 4): Open House (Dec. 8); Lotería Night (Dec. 12); Brunch with Santa (Dec. 13). These events strengthened community engagement, increased center visibility, and promoted ongoing programming. Looking Ahead – January 2026 Southwest Panthers Basketball Season Tip-Off Vision Board Workshops: Goal setting and self-development sessions for youth and community members Lotería Nights: (Jan. 5) Hosted for the Active & Aging population and (Jan. 16): Community-wide event Stephens Community Center Star Student Afterschool Program Spring Semester registration has begun. The After-school Program for Fall. (68%). Reindeer Roundup: was held on 12/18/25 at 3:00 pm. For afterschool participants. Facility Vacancies: 3-Activity Assistants, 1-Part-Time Custodian and 1-Full Time Custodian. We still have help from the CUP while they are under Renovation. Basketball practices take place Monday – Thursday 6 – 8:30pm. Other Program: We are looking into starting a mentoring program with Parkview students. We have an overview prepared for what we have to offer with the mentorship. In January we are planning to introduce the mentorship program for Parkview students. The LRPR department held their work order meeting this month, there were about 16 in total for the meeting. Estem High School continued to hold drills, shoot around and free-throw shooting until their winter break. I am still attending various meetings/activities/events as scheduled. Continuing to assist supervisors, help with Aging & Active program as needed and attend various training courses as scheduled. The community groups are still using the outdoor basketball/tennis courts/area and other areas to do exercises, meet, and fitness as the weather permits. There is still use of the field/park…daily/weekends, family gatherings, tennis court (hopefully to be refurbished as multi-use courts) for walking and playing matches, and other activities. In 2026, both courses will significantly reduce purchasing of high-ticket items such as Golf Bags and Golf Clubs, as they do not sell well at either facility, and utilize those funds to purchase higher selling items such as Golf Balls and Gloves. Rebsamen Tennis We were fairly slow over the holiday. Had a small adult USTA tournament a couple of weekends this month with about 25 players – not bad for as cold as it was. ATA has used our courts on two Sundays for state tournaments (they also used Burns Park since they have more courts there). Golf cart is broken and has been picked up and still in North Little Rock to be fixed (waiting to hear). USTA Team Tennis (Tri-level and mixed seasons) finishing up. We had 15 tri-level teams and 60 mixed doubles teams. USTA Team Triple Threat season started in early November and goes through the beginning of the year. USTA Singles leagues began early November as well and goes through mid-January. Putting together a grant proposal through the USTA to help with court resurfacing. Will continue to bid for tournament in the coming months. Museum of Arkansas Military History Museum monthly attendance for December was 1,635. This number includes: (1) on-site visitation, (2) special events, (3) virtual programming through the museum's mini-documentaries and interviews, and (4) off-site programming and outreach. On-site visitation includes 498 walk-in guests and 565 visitors to special events, meetings, tours, etc. In addition to Arkansas, visitors have come from 21 states, including Alabama, Arizona, California, Colorado, Florida, Georgia, Illinois, Kansas, Louisiana, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Missouri, New Jersey, North Carolina, Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, Tennessee, Texas, Utah, and Virginia, as well as Australia, Mexico, and Germany. Off-site programming reached a total of 275 individuals during December, while the museum's virtual programming received 297 new views. Overall attendance thus far in 2025 totals 6 35,403, which is 102% of the museum's goal. During 2025, a total of 17,834 guests participated in onsite visitation and special events (50%), 5,974 views of virtual programming (17%) and 11,595 reached through off-site outreach and programming (33%). The museum received $11,038.50 in donations in December, including $10,210 in sponsorships for the Thomas Hart Benton exhibit. Total fundraising for 2025 was $63,575: this amount more than doubles the annual goal of raising $30,000. Since 2016 the museum has raised over $612,500 in outside funding through grants, sponsorships and donations. Gift shop sales for the year were $12,327.31, exceeding the 2025 goal by 8% and setting a record for highest gift shop sales in a single year since the museum opened in 2001. Museum programmers Shane Lind and David Collins continue weekly Afterschool Programming at Stephens and Dunbar Community Centers, as well as monthly programming to students in the 21st Century program at JA Fair Preparatory Academy. During December, a total of 169 students were reached through programming at the Community Centers in addition to 31 students at J.A. Fair. So far this Fall, a total of 1077 students have been reached at the sites: (1) Dunbar Community Center – 534, (2) Stephens Community Center – 391, and (3) J.A. Fair Preparatory Academy – 152. Thomas Hart Benton, a traveling exhibit from the Naval History and Heritage Command in Washington DC, continues to receive favorable response from the public. It features 25 original paintings and drawings depicting naval scenes on board the submarine USS Dorado and LSTs along the Ohio and Mississippi Rivers. These artworks were commissioned by Abbott Laboratories and turned over to the Navy after the war. The exhibit will remain on display through July 31. The museum hosted three holiday concerts during December. Forty-four people attended the concert of the 106th Army Band's "Low Brass" ensemble group on December 6. Thirty persons attended the “Jazz, Jingles and Joy,” concert featuring the Jacksonville High School Choir on December 13. Fortythree people attended the annual holiday concert featuring students from the Margaret Wyatt Piano and Vocal Studio on December 21. The museum’s “Movies at MacArthur” film series resumes in January, which marks the program’s twelfth year. Since starting in 2015, a total of 3,918 people has attended one or more screenings of movies depicting various topics in our state and nation’s military history. The 2026 movie schedule has been finalized and is attached, as well as a flyer for the January 20 film, Miles, Morale and Memory: Bob Hope and World War II. The museum hosted the following school groups/tours in December: 182 4th grade students, parents and teachers from Sheridan on December 9 24 students and parents from Cornerstone Christian Academy in Tillar on December 9 96 7th grade students, parents and teachers from Goza Middle School in Arkadelphia on December 12 Programs and Special Events Coming Up January - March: January 20 – Movies at MacArthur, Miles, Morale and Memories: Bob Hope and World War II, 6:30 – 8:30 pm January 25 – Lecture and Book Signing with Sherman Fleek, author of MacArthur and West Point: How the General and the Academy Shaped Each Other, 2 pm January 27 – Lecture and Book Signing with David Sesser, author of The Little Rock Arsenal Crisis: On the Precipice of the American Civil War, 7 – 8 pm February 17 – Movies at MacArthur, Black Patriots: Buffalo Soldiers, 6:30 – 8 pm February 22 – Vintage Military Gear Show, 1:00 – 5:00 pm March 7 – Lecture, French Arkansas, with Dr, Nate Marvin, Francophonie Festival, 2 pm March 12 - Lecture, Revolutionary Warfare: How the Algerian War Made Modern Counterinsurgency, with Dr. Terrence G. Peterson, 6 – 7:30 pm March 17 – Movies at MacArthur, The Donut Dollies: 627 Women Who Also Served in Vietnam, 6:30 – 8 pm March 24 – “An Evening with Curt Fields as General Ulysses S. Grant,” 7 – 9 pm 7 March 25 – “An Evening with Curt Fields as President Ulysses S. Grant,” 7 – 9 pm Outdoor Recreation Outdoor Recreation Facebook page has 585 followers and has shown consistent growth on a weekly basis. The War Memorial Disc Golf project is moving forward. A preliminary course design has been established and will be presented to the public for feedback at a disc golf pop-up event in early 2026. Meetings have been set for early January to discuss pop-up dates, public interest meetings and course construction dates. The 2026 dates for the 3rd annual Squatch Till You Drop trail running event have been set and been released to the public as a “save the date” post on Facebook. Outdoor Recreation is working with the Grants department to explore possible funding sources. I completed all Cyber Security trainings to date. Lunchtime mtn bike rides on the new trails at Allsopp started in October. Rides are scheduled for 12pm-1pm on Tuesdays and 11am-12pm on Thursdays. Rides have been held most weeks (weather cancelations and Holidays are the exception). I have coordinated with city Homeless Advocates to provide assistance to members of our unsheltered community in and around War Memorial Park. This is an ongoing situation. 8

Exercise caution when clicking links, opening attachments or taking further action, before validating its authenticity. 7 Leland: I wanted to take a moment to recognize two members of your team, Adam Gadberry and Kevin, for the outstanding work they recently did at the bench and flower bed area in Allsopp Park. As I have mentioned to you before, I am part of an Adopt-A-Flowerbed group that maintains the area around a memorial bench in the park. We wanted to refresh the bed for the summer by getting more plants, soil, and mulch, and I was told that Adam would be the best person to contact about that. Adam was not familiar with the area I was talking about since he had most recently been working downtown, but he immediately offered to meet me at the bench to see it firsthand. During that visit, he shared several ideas for improving the space, including ways to better define the flower bed, build up the area so we would have more soil to work with, and he recommended colorful plants that could survive the summer heat and sun. Adam worked on this with me over the past three weeks, and the results are fantastic! Throughout the entire process, Adam was very responsive to my emails, calls, and texts and was consistently friendly and helpful. He kept me updated on what they would be doing and when, and he never made me feel like I was being a pest or inconveniencing him, which you and I both know I probably was. Several members of our flower bed group regularly run or hike through Allsopp Park in the mornings, and if Adam saw them stopped at the bench, he took the time to talk with them and share updates about the project. Every person who spoke with him later commented on how friendly and kind he was. One of the first people Adam met at the bench was my friend, Melody. She and her husband installed the bench last summer in memory of their son, Sam. The rest of us then adopted the surrounding area as a flower bed as a way to support them. When Adam described their exchange to me and mentioned that she got a little teary, I told him who she was and how much that bench and garden area have meant to them. I could tell it resonated with him. He told me later that when he saw her down there again, he pointed her out to his crew so they would know that people care about the work they do and that it really does mean something. Melody has since told me several times how touched she is by the kindness and effort shown by everyone working on the project, particularly Adam. She appreciates not only the quality of the work, but also the compassion and care that the crew demonstrated while making an already meaningful place even more special. She absolutely loves it. As I told you before, I know we were extremely fortunate to catch Adam while so much work was being done on the playground area, but he still went above and beyond. Despite everything else on his plate, he devoted time and attention to our project. He even went to three different nurseries to find the canna lilies he wanted us to use! And when he delivered them to me, he asked if I thought Melody would like them. It was so 8 thoughtful and another example of how much he genuinely cared about the project and its impact on people who cared about Sam. I also want to give a shoutout to Kevin, whose last name I unfortunately do not know. (He has a beard and appears to be in his forties, maybe?) I spoke with him several times at the park and he was always friendly and eager to help with a big smile on his face. Kevin is a hard worker and moved several large rocks, trimmed a few tree branches around the area, and even created a deeper pool in the creek to make it easier for our volunteers to fill water jugs when caring for the flower bed. Like Adam, he seemed genuinely happy to help us. The improvements to the bench area are wonderful, but what stands out most to me is the incredible kindness and genuine care that Adam, Kevin, and the rest of the crew demonstrated throughout the process. Their work made a visible difference in the park, but their generosity and kindness made an even greater impression on the people who love and care for this special place. Although I told them myself, please pass along my sincere thanks and appreciation to both of them. You are lucky to have them representing the Little Rock Parks Department, and I wanted to make sure their efforts did not go unnoticed. Thank you, Mary Ellen P.S. I am attaching a couple of photos for you. One is from March, where you can see we had some pansies, muhly grass, and two dwarf crepe myrtles (which you cannot see behind the bench) planted in the area. Adam’s crew dug that up, put down big rocks that they repurposed from somewhere else in the park, unloaded some more soil, and replanted the crepe myrtles. Our group gathered the smaller rocks from the creek and placed them, then planted the bee balm, blanket flowers, and lilies that Adam brought us. Adam sent me a picture after they added mulch yesterday. As you can see, it is quite an improvement.
